concepts.def: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj — for right-angled triangles.
Sides labelled relative to a chosen angle (not the right angle).
Use inverse functions (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) on the ratio.
sin 30° = 1/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 45° = 1; useful exact ratios.
a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C — for any triangle.
a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A — for any triangle when you have SAS or SSS.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Trigonometry — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Trigonometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Trigonometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
